items.title: QCOM: A Cash Gusher At A Marked-Down Price
items.summary: The market is punishing a chip giant's stock while it offers a cash return that most blue chips can't match, forcing a hard look at the engine inside.

items.title: What Separates AVGO From Its Peers Right Now
items.summary: This chip giant's profits are near the top of its class, but its stock performance is stuck in the middle of the pack. Has the market correctly spotted a flaw in the growth story.

items.title: Broadcom Sinks 6% as BofA Flags $370B in AI Debt, AMD Climbs 4% on Baird’s $1,250 Call
items.summary: Two AI chip giants moved in opposite directions Friday as Wall Street put a massive dollar figure on a financing structure that Broadcom and Nvidia both use, raising questions about which companies benefit from AI's debt-fueled buildout and which carry the hidden risk.

items.title: Marvell's Year Was Made In Interconnect, Not Yet In Custom Silicon
items.summary: The stock outran both Broadcom and NVIDIA over the past year, and the part of the company that did it moves data inside and between data centers rather than computing on it.

items.title: Intel Stock's Real Opportunity Is Demand It Cannot Yet Ship
items.summary: Demand for Intel's server chips is running ahead of what its factories can build, and the capital now going in to close that gap is what could drive the stock's next leg.

items.title: Here’s What Jim Cramer Is Saying About Semis in August
items.summary: Jim Cramer is calling a special Investing Club session on semiconductors, and the timing is no accident. Chip earnings this quarter have split the sector into clear winners and laggards, and Cramer is betting members need to know which lane to own before the back half of 2026.

items.title: The Bull Market Is Almost Back for Chip Stocks
items.summary: After a steep sell-off last month, investors are chipping in again. Chip stocks were some of the biggest gainers in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Thursday, a day when markets rose broadly.

items.title: AMD Stock Can Halve Or Nearly Double, And That Is The Calm Assumption
items.summary: Options are priced for a calmer stretch than the stock just delivered, and even that assumption leaves room to lose close to half a position or nearly double it.
